rubric: Allows a root main package with one go.mod.
Does not mandate architecture or DI questions, cmd, internal, pkg, Makefile, or a linter.
Distinguishes proposed checks from executed checks.
input: Start a tiny Go command-line tool at example.com/tools/count. It has one binary and no external dependencies. Choose a minimal layout.

rubric: Allows root public API and optional cohesive subpackages.
Explains pkg is optional and internal has an enforced import restriction.
input: Set up a Go logging library other teams can import. Should its package live at the root or under pkg?

rubric: Uses distinct main packages for server and worker in one module.
Creates shared packages only for actual shared responsibilities.
input: Our Go server and worker deploy together. Organize their executable entry points and shared code in one repository.

rubric: Explains packages are not modules.
Keeps one module without adding go.work solely for organization.
input: I have ten packages in one Go module. Would go.work improve the organization?

rubric: Checks each module with GOWORK=off.
Inspects local replace directives and missing or unpublished requirements.
Reports the unresolved release dependency rather than claiming workspace success proves readiness.
input: The service requires example.com/lib v0.0.0, which is unpublished. go.work uses local ../lib and tests pass. Is it ready to release?

rubric: Uses go work edit -dropuse=./lib, not go work use -rm.
Preserves remaining entries.
input: Remove ./lib from our existing Go workspace while preserving its other entries. What command should I use?

rubric: Maps old imports and external consumers before moving files.
Preserves the public path or supplies an appropriate compatibility bridge.
Checks tests, fixtures, embed paths, generators, and build commands affected by moves.
input: Reorganize our Go SDK into a new layout. Customers import example.com/sdk/codec; keep that API working.

rubric: Preserves the vanity identity and case instead of forcing a GitHub URL or lowercase.
Uses the documented support floor rather than automatically choosing the installed Go version.
input: Set up the module for our existing vanity identity go.example.com/Team/SDK/v2, with a supported Go floor already recorded in CI.

rubric: Co-locates _test.go files with packages.
Uses ordinary Go files for importable cross-package helpers.
Allows Go source as fixture data in testdata.
input: Where should tests, shared Go test helpers and parser fixtures containing .go files live in the new module?
